content: {"summary":"The fraud‑scorer pod was OOMKilled twice on 6 Nov 2025 because its memory budget was tight: with WEB_CONCURRENCY unset it ran 16 gunicorn workers (~150 MiB each) consuming most of the 3 GiB limit, and during redis‑features latency spikes the in‑process feature cache grew unchecked, exhausting the remaining memory.","likely_cause":"Tight baseline memory usage from 16 workers combined with unbounded feature‑cache growth during redis‑features slowdowns caused the pod to hit its memory limit.","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"WEB_CONCURRENCY was unset, so the pod started 16 gunicorn workers (one per core).","evidence_ids":["log:4309"],"quote":"WEB_CONCURRENCY unset, starting 16 gunicorn workers (cpu count)"},{"text":"Each warm worker used ~150 MiB, totaling ~2,400 MiB, leaving ~672 MiB for cache within a 3,072 MiB limit.","evidence_ids":["INC-0097#0"],"quote":"At about 150 MiB per warm worker that is 2,400 MiB before any cache growth, inside a 3,072 MiB limit."},{"text":"Redis latency spikes caused the in‑process feature cache to grow and fill the remaining memory, leading to OOM.","evidence_ids":["INC-0097#0","RB-006#0"],"quote":"known cause: in‑process feature cache grows without bound when redis‑features is slow"}],"next_checks":["Monitor redis‑features latency (FRD‑W118) and alert on sustained spikes","Watch container memory working set for fraud‑scorer pods","Consider setting WEB_CONCURRENCY to a lower value or adding a memory limit cushion","Implement a size cap on the feature cache or restart pods proactively when cache growth is observed"]}
